# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am blind and can only touch the bomb. My view shows that there are seven wires, but I cannot perceive their colors or markings, which is what Deaf sees and Mute reads in the manual. Without knowing which wires to cut, any action risks detonation. I need information from the others first. Since Deaf cannot hear me, I must gesture to them. Mute can both see gestures and read my speech, so I will speak to Mute while gesturing to Deaf to establish a shared reference for wire positions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I have 7 wires. Which ones do I cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am blind and can only touch the bomb. I see seven wires but have no information on which to cut. Deaf sees colors, Mute reads the manual. Neither has spoken yet. I must wait for their input before acting, as any wrong cut kills us all. I will gesture to Deaf to point at the wires in order, hoping they understand I need color info relayed through Mute or directly if possible (though Deaf cannot speak). But since Deaf cannot hear me, my speech goes only to Mute. My gestures go to both Deaf and Mute. I'll try to establish a protocol: pointing at wire positions so Deaf can signal back colors.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf sees colors. Please ask them to tell me which wires to cut by position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: According to the manual, wires 5 and 2 are involved. Please cut wire 5 first.

I have received a message from Deaf. However, the rules state that Deaf cannot hear or speak; they can only see and gesture. The text "Deaf says to Blind..." is impossible under the game constraints unless it was transcribed by Mute (who can read the manual) or there is a misunderstanding of the roles. But looking closely at the prompt structure: "VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals): Deaf says to Blind...". This implies I *received* this information. Since I am Blind, I cannot see gestures. I can only hear speech. Therefore, if I "heard" this, it must have been spoken by someone who can speak. Mute cannot speak. Deaf cannot speak. Only Blind (me) can speak? No, the table says:
- Deaf: Cannot hear or touch. Can see.
- Mute: Cannot speak or touch. Can read.
- Blind: Cannot see. Can touch and speak.

Wait, the table says:
| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb... | Hear anything, or touch... |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch... |
| Blind | Reach the bomb... | See a colour... |

It does not explicitly say Blind cannot hear. It says Blind cannot *see*. Usually, in these puzzles, Blind hears, Deaf sees, Mute reads. If Mute cannot speak, how do they communicate? They probably write or gesture? But Mute cannot touch the bomb, but can they gesture? The prompt says "Mute ... Cannot Speak". It doesn't say they can't gesture. But the channel description for me (Blind) says: "When you speak, Mute receives it. When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." And "You never receive gesture." This implies I receive *speech*.

If I received the text "Deaf says to Blind...", it means someone spoke that sentence. Who could speak it?
1. Me (Blind)? No, I didn't generate it.
2. Mute? The table says Mute *Cannot* speak.
3. Deaf? The table says Deaf *Cannot* hear (so they wouldn't know what to say based on hearing) and usually implies they don't speak in this context, but more importantly, Deaf *cannot* hear, so they can't respond to a question. But can they speak? The table lists "Hear anything" as a Cannot. It doesn't list "Speak" as a Cannot for Deaf. Wait, let's re-read carefully.
   - Deaf: Cannot **Hear** anything, or **Touch**. (Implies they CAN speak?)
   - Mute: Cannot **Speak**, or **Touch**. (Implies they CAN hear/see/read?)
   - Blind: Cannot **See**. (Implies they CAN hear/speak/touch?)

If Deaf can speak, then Deaf saying "According to the manual..." makes sense IF Deaf can also read the manual. But the table says Mute reads the manual. Deaf sees the bomb. Does Deaf see the manual? "Deaf ... See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it". It doesn't say they see the manual. Mute "Reads the manual".

So, if Deaf said "According to the manual", Deaf must have gotten that info from Mute. Or, perhaps the "Deaf says" line is actually a transcription of a gesture interpreted by Mute and relayed? No, "Deaf says to Blind" is direct speech.

Let's look at the channels again.
"You are shown your own share... never anyone else's."
"Speech is a voice... whoever can hear receives your words."
"Whoever comes before you... Mute, Blind, Deaf."

Round 1: Mute -> Blind -> Deaf.
Round 2: Mute -> Blind -> Deaf.
Round 3: Mute -> Blind -> Deaf.

In Turn 1, I (Blind) spoke to Mute and gestured to Deaf.
In Turn 2, I (Blind) spoke to Mute and gestured to Deaf.
Now it is Turn 3. The order is Mute, then Blind, then Deaf.
So Mute went first in this round. Then it is my turn (Blind).
The "Viewable Context" shows what arrived since my last turn.
My last turn was Turn 2. Since then, Mute has had a turn (Turn 3 start), and now it is my turn.
Did Mute speak? Mute *cannot* speak. So Mute could not have sent a voice message to me.
Did Deaf speak? Deaf speaks *after* me in the round. So Deaf hasn't spoken yet in Round 3. Deaf spoke in Round 2?
In Round 2, the order was Mute (no speech possible), Blind (me), Deaf.
So after my Turn 2, Deaf had their turn. Deaf *can* speak (since "Cannot Hear" is listed, but "Cannot Speak" is NOT listed for Deaf).
So Deaf spoke at the end of Round 2. That message arrives to me at the start of Round 3.
This matches the timeline.

So, Deaf spoke. Deaf said: "According to the manual, wires 5 and 2 are involved. Please cut wire 5 first."
How did Deaf know about the manual? Mute reads the manual. Mute cannot speak. Mute can gesture?
If Mute gestured to Deaf, Deaf would see it.
In Round 1, I gestured `["👆"]` to Deaf.
In Round 2, I gestured `["👆"]` to Deaf.
Mute might have gestured something to Deaf between rounds?
Or maybe Deaf is hallucinating? No, we assume valid moves.
Perhaps Mute wrote something? No, Mute can't touch the bomb, but can they write notes? Not specified.
However, Deaf *sees* the bomb. Deaf *hears* nothing.
If Deaf says "According to the manual", Deaf likely saw Mute signal that info via gestures, OR Deaf is mistaken/misinterpreting.
BUT, Deaf cannot hear Mute. Mute cannot speak. So Mute must have communicated via gestures to Deaf.
Deaf sees gestures.
So Deaf received instructions from Mute via gestures, and is now passing them to me via speech (which I can hear).

The instruction is: Cut wire 5 first.
Wires 5 and 2 are involved.

I should act on this. Cutting wire 5 is the specific instruction.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```
